sections.title: UI Foundations · Token architecture
sections.text:
UI Foundations · Token architecture
Private UIF proof of concept · Updated 30 September 2026
Core → Appearance {Brand, Scheme, Scale} → Semantics → Patterns

This README describes the bounded migration in this branch. The Vault ADR is in review. The owner’s instruction authorizes this experiment; general adoption still follows the Vault lifecycle. UIF remains separate from UILib and the official TUI Design System.

sections.title: 01 / Collections and responsibilities
sections.text:
01 / Collections and responsibilities
Core (Primitives) — Literal colors, spacing, typography and radius primitives. One default mode.

Appearance (Brand) — Identity, palette selection, typography and shape. Brand A / Brand B / Brand C.

Appearance (Scheme) — Light and dark realizations. Light Mode / Dark Mode.

Appearance (Scale) — Scalar projections and fluid endpoints. Min / Max.

Semantics (Roles) — Reusable purpose and state contracts. One default mode.

Patterns (UI) — Component family, variant, part, property and state slots. One Component mode.

Interaction (States) — Four prototype helpers. Explicitly excluded from the foundation contract and Runtime projection.

sections.title: 02 / Dependency flow
sections.text:
02 / Dependency flow
Arrows in the architecture show increasing abstraction. Variable aliases point back toward their dependencies.

Patterns consume Semantics. Semantics consume Appearance. Brand and Scale can reference Core; Scheme can reference Brand or Core. Brand, Scheme and Scale are separate context axes. The semantic layer adds purpose without selecting a brand or scheme.
Pattern slot → Semantic role → Appearance mapping → Core primitive

Brand × Scheme = 3 × 2 contexts
Scale Min / Max = interpolation endpoints

sections.title: 03 / Deterministic naming
sections.text:
03 / Deterministic naming
Use slash-delimited Figma names and dot-delimited logical paths. Token names contain no free-form whitespace. Keep interaction state last. Optional variant and part segments depend on the family. Size variants are a separate property axis.

Active is the existing contract name for pressed behavior. Default, Hover, Active and Focus remain separately addressable, even when values match.
Color/<purpose>/<role>/<state>
<family>/<variant?>/<part?>/<property>/<state?>

Color/Action/Surface/Hover
Color/Action/Content/Hover
Button/Solid/Container/Background/Hover
Shape/Corner/Control

sections.title: 04 / Brand and Scheme
sections.text:
04 / Brand and Scheme
Brand owns identity and shape choices. Scheme resolves light/dark appearance. These axes stay independent; switching Scheme must not silently select a different Brand.

Core’s qualified Brand A/B/C source palettes identify private provenance. They do not define reusable UI purpose. Preserve their current values; UILib-specific brand values are outside UIF.

sections.title: 05 / Scale and fluid typography
sections.text:
05 / Scale and fluid typography
Min and Max are endpoints, not light/dark modes. Runtime projects the actual Figma endpoints into a global fluid clamp. Scalar Appearance bridges allow Semantics to consume Core values without bypassing the Appearance layer.

The former code-only Liquid curve is retired in migration evidence. The corrected lg curve is 20–36px; responsive rendering can therefore differ from the former 18–20px curve.
Font size      Min → Max      Line height      Min → Max
lg             20 → 36px      lg               28 → 44px
xl             24 → 40px      xl               32 → 48px
xxl            32 → 48px      xxl              44 → 60px
xxxl           40 → 56px      xxxl             56 → 72px

sections.title: 06 / Surface ↔ Content
sections.text:
06 / Surface ↔ Content
Surface is the filled region. Content is text or an icon on that Surface. Match purpose and state when declaring a contrast pair. Verify every Brand × Scheme context and composite transparent colors over a declared background.

Normal text requires 4.5:1; large text and applicable non-text boundaries require 3:1. Disabled pairs are explicitly recorded exemptions. Structural pairing alone does not certify rendered accessibility or focus visibility.
Color/Action/Surface/Default ↔ Color/Action/Content/Default
Color/Action/Surface/Hover   ↔ Color/Action/Content/Hover
Color/Action/Surface/Active  ↔ Color/Action/Content/Active
Color/Action/Surface/Focus   ↔ Color/Action/Content/Focus

sections.title: 07 / Foreground is a separate contract
sections.text:
07 / Foreground is a separate contract
Foreground describes an independently rendered action or status mark on a surrounding surface. For example, outline and ghost button text uses Action Foreground; solid button text uses Action Content on its filled Action Surface.

Evaluate Foreground against its declared surrounding surface. Do not substitute Content and Foreground just because a current color looks similar.
Solid text   → Color/Action/Content/Default
Outline text → Color/Action/Foreground/Default
Ghost text   → Color/Action/Foreground/Default

sections.title: 08 / Brand-owned shape
sections.text:
08 / Brand-owned shape
Brand owns corner choices. Semantics exposes reusable purpose. Patterns share those roles rather than aliasing another component’s radius. Existing brand values and public CSS names remain compatible.
Legacy brand choice → Brand shape purpose → Semantic role
Button              → Control             → Shape/Corner/Control
Card                → Panel               → Shape/Corner/Panel
Modal               → Dialog              → Shape/Corner/Dialog
Input               → Field               → Shape/Corner/Field
Container           → Container           → Shape/Corner/Container
Tooltip             → Floating            → Shape/Corner/Floating

sections.title: 09 / Scoped variables
sections.text:
09 / Scoped variables
Surface → Frame / Shape fills
Content → Text / Shape fills
Foreground → Text / Shape fills and Stroke color
Borders → Stroke color
Shape → Corner radius
Typography → Font size, weight or line height as appropriate
Spacing → Gap or dimensions according to actual use

Shared low-level palettes may use ALL_FILLS and STROKE_COLOR. Unclassified helpers retain recorded exceptions. Do not restrict a scope in a way that invalidates an existing binding.

sections.title: 10 / Live Button aliases
sections.text:
10 / Live Button aliases
These examples were checked against the current variable graph. The border radius resolves to the reusable Control shape role.
Button/Solid/Container/Background/Default
  → Color/Action/Surface/Default
Button/Solid/Container/Background/Hover
  → Color/Action/Surface/Hover
Button/Solid/Text/Color/Default
  → Color/Action/Content/Default
Button/Outline/Text/Color/Default
  → Color/Action/Foreground/Default
Button/Ghost/Text/Color/Default
  → Color/Action/Foreground/Default
Button/Border/Radius
  → Shape/Corner/Control

sections.title: 11 / Runtime projection and compatibility
sections.text:
11 / Runtime projection and compatibility
Variable IDs are the stable mapping keys. Explicit codeSyntax.WEB and existing CSS/export paths remain compatibility contracts. Figma display names can evolve through the recorded adapter without guessing aliases from a name.

New semantic properties use --uif-semantic-*; new Appearance bridge properties use --uif-appearance-*. Compatible export filenames can retain older collection labels. Semantics exports are qualified to avoid collisions with Scheme.
Canonical adapter: figma/token-projection.json
Existing WEB syntax example: var(--uif-button-border-radius)
Synchronization: ID → current Figma name → compatible export path

sections.title: 12 / Verification and open accessibility defects
sections.text:
12 / Verification and open accessibility defects
Structure and projection: PASS. All 641 original variables are preserved. The branch now has 765 variables: 99 semantic roles and 25 Appearance bridges added. All 296 Pattern alias connections consume Roles. Runtime projects 761 variables; four prototype helpers are excluded. Resolved values are unchanged across 7,692 context comparisons.

Runtime lint, 182 unit tests and the bounded Chromium check passed.

Accessibility: FAIL. Surface/Content checks: 58 pass, 6 exempt, 14 fail. Action Foreground: 12 pass, 12 fail. Composited action overlays: 9 pass, 3 fail.

Base Action Surface/Content pairs pass in all six Brand × Scheme contexts. Existing defects remain in Brand B status/subtle/selection, dark Action Foreground and dark Hover/Active overlays. Architecture parity is not accessibility certification. Rendered components and screenreader behavior need their own evidence.

sections.title: 13 / Authority, evidence and review
sections.text:
13 / Authority, evidence and review
Durable decision: UIF-VLT / adr.token-model-and-figma-projection · Status: review.
Runtime contract and reproducible evidence: UIF-RUN / figma/migrations/token-model-2026-09-30/.

The bounded slice preserves IDs, WEB syntax and existing visual values. Recorded legacy exceptions include literal Pattern slots and code-only projections. Broader palette repair, component geometry changes, releases and Figma library publication are separate work.

Vault and Runtime remain distinct responsibilities. This document is a Figma projection of the Vault decision, not a second governance source.
Vault ADR review: github.com/tbielich/ui-foundations-vault/pull/49
Runtime projection review: github.com/tbielich/ui-foundations-runtime/pull/313
